GAP-TRANSLATION-004.note: Expected re-declared from 2 to 36 after R4-REVERT-01. The literal measure counts a verse's OWN edge and so cannot reach 0 without reintroducing GAP-TRANSLATION-006. 34 of the 36 now carry a typed translation_coverage row naming their anchor.

GAP-TRANSLATION-006-not-regressed.measure: even-numbered verses in RV 1.65-1.70 carrying a HAS_TRANSLATION edge

post_migration_corrections.what: Deleted all 34 HAS_TRANSLATION edges GAP-TRANSLATION-004 created.
post_migration_corrections.why: A cross-gap regression this migration caused and the registry re-measure caught. GAP-TRANSLATION-006 exists because Griffith numbers each four-pada group as one verse where this graph numbers each hemistich, so 25 of 31 shipped translations in RV 1.65-1.70 read against the wrong Sanskrit; the fix was to REMOVE the rendering from the even-numbered hemistichs, and its closure measure asks for 0 even verses in that span carrying a HAS_TRANSLATION edge. 30 of the 34 edges staged here landed on exactly those verses and drove that measure 0 -> 30, reintroducing the defect. The premise was wrong: 'covered by a declared range' is expressed on the ANCHOR's Translation node, deliberately, and making it reachable from the covered verse shows a reader the wrong Sanskrit's rendering.
post_migration_corrections.kept: The 36 per-mantra translation_coverage rows and the 4 anchor re-types to MANTRA_RANGE. Those are disclosure and scope declaration; neither attaches a rendering to a verse it does not render.

delta_against_the_r4_baseline.why: census_before in this receipt was taken after a partial first run that failed on a profile property name, so the delta above is relative to that intermediate state. This block is relative to the R4 baseline the brief states, which is what a reader wants.
